claims.text: A data-driven machine-learning framework can rapidly predict refractory HEA compositions.
The proposed framework integrates atomic-scale descriptors with historical composition-property data.
The proposed machine-learning framework can identify alloys having intrinsic strength, ductility, and low weight simultaneously.
Refractory high-entropy alloys are composed of multiple principal refractory elements.
Refractory high-entropy alloys typically form disordered BCC or related matrices.
The machine-learning model should be trained on a curated database containing compositions, processing parameters, and experimental or simulated properties.
High-throughput computational screening can rapidly explore a large HEA composition space.
Configurational entropy, atomic radii, valence-electron concentration, and density are suitable inputs for the proposed model.
Configurational entropy, atomic-size mismatch, valence-electron concentration, and density mediate microstructural features and mechanical performance.
The machine-learning framework learns nonlinear correlations between compositional descriptors and mechanical outcomes.
Learned descriptor-property correlations enable prediction of compositions balancing strength, ductility, and low density.
The proposed machine-learning approach avoids iterative, time-consuming thermo-kinetic simulations.
The proposed approach will yield RHEA candidates with greater intrinsic strength and ductility and lower density than alloys designed by conventional methods.
High-throughput computational design can accelerate discovery of light and strong HEAs.
The very large HEA compositional space creates a need for advanced and efficient alloy-design tools.
Traditional thermo-kinetic and iterative experimental methods are slower and less capable of exploring HEA compositional space than the proposed machine-learning method.
The success and predictive accuracy of the method depend on the availability and quality of its data.
Sparse observations and unaccounted processing variables may limit predictive accuracy.
The proposed model may overfit an incomplete training dataset.
Translation from a predicted composition to a manufacturable alloy with real-world performance remains unvalidated.

contradictions.description: The conditions call for screening under simulated thermo-kinetic conditions, while the mechanism says the method enables prediction without iterative thermo-kinetic simulations. The distinction between using such simulations as inputs and avoiding them during design is not clarified.
